Since you are oriented towards bugs, know this: DEET can be very harmful to your health if over-used. It appears your locale is warm and wet; there is much wildlife in areas of the type. I live in such a place. Natural anti-bug stuff doesn't work well; what I've been using for years now is "sheep dip" that contains permethrin (NOT pyrethrin). I spray clothing and shoes, allow it to dry, and put 'em on. Prior to that, used DEET and anything else I could find, and a walk in my woods yielded dozens of ticks and other biting critters. With the permethrin, that is cut down to one or two. Occasionally, I spray my shoes and socks with me in them - hasn't done any harm. Keep in mind permethrin is for animals and animal bedding, and is not harmful unless you happen to be allergic. This works.

Now, allow me to state that I grew up spending much time in the woods of Montana. I'm old. I am a Vietnam vet, USN, helo aircrew. As such, I was required to go through all the stupid SERE schools, jungle survival and all that. So... I will say this: more is better. None of the instruction I got in the navy was particularly enlightening, other than having the shit beat out of me in SERE POW camp. Where I learned almost everything was from two very experienced woodsmen - my Dad and an ancient Blackfoot. Their teaching was as much by experience as instruction.

Spend as much time doing different builds as possible. Get the hell off the ground, use branches with greenery stacked for bedding. Know the green stuff out there - find a book that covers your area. You MUST know the plants, because they can kill you as readily as a griz; more so if you don't know them.

Your fire doesn't have to be that big. For heating, you can build a reflector from local materials similar to your lean-to, but have it angled so the fire heat reflects into the lean-to. If you want you can cover it with foil; keep it far enough away to avoid burning it.

Careful of your crossbar. Looks as if your roof is heavier than need be, and that crossbar isn't big enough. Practice helps a lot.
